transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah—so, I guess what finally made me come in is work stuff. I work in meat processing, and there are these sanitation steps and batch logs and end-of-line paperwork that have to be done exactly right, and I’ll start them, I really will, but somehow I leave off the last parts. Like I know they matter, I know my job depends on finishing them correctly, and still I miss the ending.

It’s frustrating because it’s not like I don’t care. I’ll be in the middle of it, and then something else on the line happens, or I think I finished because I did most of it, and then later it turns out I didn’t. And then I feel awful because it looks careless. That’s kind of what pushed me to make the appointment.
Outside of work, do you find yourself starting tasks but not finishing them, or getting easily distracted in other areas of your life?

Yeah, I mean… I notice it most at work, honestly. Like the sanitation steps or batch logs or the end-of-line paperwork—I’ll start them, and I think I’m doing it, but then somehow the last parts just don’t get done. Even though I know it’s important, like really important, and my job depends on it.

Outside work… sorry, I’m trying not to ramble. It’s just that at work it’s the clearest because there’s paperwork showing what I missed. Like I’ll get through most of it and then something pulls me away, or I assume I’m finished, and then later it’s like, no, I left out the end again.
When you’re at home or in other settings outside of work, do you find it hard to stay focused on tasks like chores, conversations, or hobbies, or do you often get distracted by things around you?

Yeah, I mean… at home it’s harder for me to pin down, because there isn’t like a log sheet proving I messed up, you know? But the focus thing does happen. Like even when I start a shift telling myself, okay, stay locked in, pay attention, don’t drift—after a while the cutting and weighing and checking labels all kind of blur together.

And then I’ll realize I’m just staring at the same tray or the same log sheet, like I’m looking at it but not actually taking in what I’m supposed to do next. It’s weird, because I’m technically there, I’m not off somewhere else, but my brain just… stops following the steps. I guess that’s why I keep bringing it back to work, sorry. It’s just the clearest place I notice it.
When you're at home doing things like chores, watching TV, or talking with family, do you find yourself zoning out, losing focus, or having trouble staying attentive?

Yeah, I guess it’s kind of the same thing, though I notice it more at work than at home. Like even when I start a shift really trying to stay locked in—telling myself, okay, pay attention—the cutting and weighing and checking labels all start to blur together after a while.

And then I’ll catch myself just… staring at the same tray, or the same log sheet, and I’m not actually taking in what I’m supposed to do next. Sorry, I know you asked about home. It’s just the clearest example I can think of, because at work there’s something concrete in front of me showing I lost the thread.
When you're at home, like when you're watching TV or talking with family, do you find yourself zoning out or having trouble staying focused even when there's no pressure or paperwork involved?

Yeah… I mean, I think so, but the example that keeps coming to mind is still work. Like I’ll start a shift really trying to stay locked in—like, okay, focus, don’t mess this up—and after a while the cutting and weighing and checking labels just kind of blend together.

Then I realize I’ve been staring at the same tray, or the same log sheet, and I’m not actually taking in what I’m supposed to do next. It’s not like I’m choosing to ignore it, I just sort of lose the thread. At home there isn’t a log sheet, so it’s harder for me to point to, but that zoning-out feeling is similar.

Outside of work, when you’re doing things like watching TV, talking with family, or doing chores, do you ever catch yourself zoning out or losing focus, even when there’s no pressure or specific tasks to complete?

Yeah, I mean… outside work I think it happens, but it’s harder for me to separate because there isn’t, like, something obvious showing I drifted. The clearest version is still at work, honestly.

Like I can start a shift really trying to stay locked in, telling myself to focus, and then after a while the cutting, weighing, checking labels—it all just sort of blends together. And then I’ll realize I’m staring at the same tray or the same log sheet and I’m not actually taking in what I’m supposed to do next.

So yeah, that same zoning-out feeling happens, but I notice it most when there’s a task in front of me and I can see that I lost the thread.
When you're at home, like when you're watching TV or talking with family, do you catch yourself zoning out or losing focus, even when there's nothing specific you need to do?

Yeah, I guess I do, but it’s weird because at home it’s harder for me to notice. Like if I’m watching something, I might realize I don’t really know what just happened, but then I’ll just rewind it or check my phone or whatever, so it doesn’t stand out as much.

The thing I keep thinking of is still work, sorry—I know you’re asking about home. But there, even when I start the shift really trying to stay focused, after a while the cutting and weighing and checking labels just kind of blur together. Then I realize I’ve been staring at the same tray or the log sheet and I’m not actually taking in what I’m supposed to do next. At home it feels kind of like that, just less obvious because nothing is really tracking it.
Have you ever been diagnosed with any medical or neurological conditions, such as seizures, sleep apnea, or anything else that might affect your attention or alertness?

Um… not that I can think of. I mean, I don’t think anyone’s ever told me I have something like that.

I’ve had normal doctor stuff here and there, like checkups, and once I got really worried about headaches during finals, but I think that was more me spiraling and not sleeping great—sorry, that’s probably not what you asked. No, I haven’t been diagnosed with seizures or sleep apnea or anything neurological that I know of.
Have you been feeling down, losing interest in things you usually enjoy, or feeling like you’re not worth much lately?

Um… I don’t know. Not really, I guess? I mean, I have days where I feel kind of useless, but I don’t know if that’s like… being down, or just getting frustrated with myself.

I still like the things I like, when I actually sit down and do them. Sometimes I’ll mean to do something fun and then I get distracted and end up just scrolling, and then suddenly it’s late, which makes me feel kind of bad. But I’m not sure if that’s what you mean by losing interest.

Sorry, I feel like I’m not answering it cleanly. I haven’t really noticed being, like, depressed lately, no.
When you're at home, like when you're watching TV or talking with family, do you often lose focus or feel like your mind is somewhere else, even when there's nothing else going on?

Yeah… I mean, yes, I do, but I notice it more in places where there’s something I’m supposed to be doing, if that makes sense.

Like at home, if I’m watching TV, I’ll realize I missed a whole scene, but then I just rewind it and it’s not a big deal. But it feels similar to what happens at work, where I’ll start a shift really trying to stay locked in, and after a while the cutting and weighing and checking labels just kind of all blur together. Then I’ll catch myself staring at the same tray or the log sheet and I’m not actually taking in what I’m supposed to do next.

So yeah, at home it happens too, just… there’s less consequence, I guess, so I don’t always notice it right away.
